import Mathlib

-- Precondition definition
@[reducible, simp]
def can_jump_precond (nums : List Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  0 < nums.length ∧
  nums.length ≤ 10000 ∧
  (∀ i, i < nums.length → nums.getD i 0 ≤ 10000)
  -- !benchmark @end precond

def is_valid_jump_path (path : List Nat) (nums : List Nat) : Prop :=
  path.length > 0 ∧
  path.head? = some 0 ∧
  path.getLast? = some (nums.length - 1) ∧
  (∀ i, i < path.length → path.getD i 0 < nums.length) ∧
  (∀ i, i < path.length - 1 →
    let u := path.getD i 0
    let v := path.getD (i+1) 0
    u < v ∧ v ≤ u + nums.getD u 0)

-- !benchmark @start auxcode

/-- `JReach nums v` : index `v` is reachable from index `0` by a sequence of legal jumps. -/
inductive JReach (nums : List Nat) : Nat → Prop
  | zero : JReach nums 0
  | step : ∀ {u v : Nat}, JReach nums u → u < v → v ≤ u + nums.getD u 0 → JReach nums v

/-- Greedy scan: `i` is the index being examined, `r` the furthest index reachable so far. -/
def jumpGo (nums : List Nat) (i r : Nat) : Nat :=
  if h : i < nums.length ∧ i ≤ r then
    jumpGo nums (i + 1) (max r (i + nums.getD i 0))
  else
    r
termination_by nums.length - i
decreasing_by
  have := h.1
  omega

/-- The step-condition of `is_valid_jump_path`, split out for convenience. -/
def jumpChain (nums : List Nat) (path : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, i < path.length - 1 →
    path.getD i 0 < path.getD (i + 1) 0 ∧
    path.getD (i + 1) 0 ≤ path.getD i 0 + nums.getD (path.getD i 0) 0

-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def can_jump (nums : List Nat) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  Nat.ble (nums.length - 1) (jumpGo nums 0 0)
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definition
@[reducible, simp]
def can_jump_postcond (nums : List Nat) (result : Bool) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (result = true) ↔ ∃ (path : List Nat), is_valid_jump_path path nums
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma

theorem jumpGo_pos (nums : List Nat) (i r : Nat) (hc : i < nums.length ∧ i ≤ r) :
    jumpGo nums i r = jumpGo nums (i + 1) (max r (i + nums.getD i 0)) := by
  rw [jumpGo, dif_pos hc]

theorem jumpGo_neg (nums : List Nat) (i r : Nat) (hc : ¬ (i < nums.length ∧ i ≤ r)) :
    jumpGo nums i r = r := by
  rw [jumpGo, dif_neg hc]

/-- Everything below the greedy bound is genuinely reachable. -/
theorem jumpGo_reach (nums : List Nat) (i r : Nat) :
    (∀ k, k ≤ r → JReach nums k) → ∀ k, k ≤ jumpGo nums i r → JReach nums k := by
  induction i, r using jumpGo.induct nums with
  | case1 i r hc ih =>
      intro h
      rw [jumpGo_pos nums i r hc]
      apply ih
      intro k hk
      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge r k with h1 | h1
      · exact JReach.step (h i hc.2) (by omega) (by omega)
      · exact h k h1
  | case2 i r hc =>
      intro h
      rw [jumpGo_neg nums i r hc]
      exact h

/-- The greedy bound absorbs every jump starting from an in-range index below it. -/
theorem jumpGo_sat (nums : List Nat) (i r : Nat) :
    (∀ u, u < i → u < nums.length → u ≤ r → u + nums.getD u 0 ≤ r) →
    ∀ u, u < nums.length → u ≤ jumpGo nums i r → u + nums.getD u 0 ≤ jumpGo nums i r := by
  induction i, r using jumpGo.induct nums with
  | case1 i r hc ih =>
      intro h
      rw [jumpGo_pos nums i r hc]
      apply ih
      intro u hu1 hu2 hu3
      rcases Nat.lt_or_ge u i with h1 | h1
      · have := h u h1 hu2 (by omega)
        omega
      · have : u = i := by omega
        subst this
        omega
  | case2 i r hc =>
      intro h
      rw [jumpGo_neg nums i r hc]
      intro u hu1 hu2
      have hi : u < i := by
        by_cases hn : i < nums.length
        · have : ¬ (i ≤ r) := by tauto
          omega
        · omega
      exact h u hi hu1 hu2

theorem getD_out (nums : List Nat) (u : Nat) (h : nums.length ≤ u) : nums.getD u 0 = 0 := by
  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_eq_none h]

/-- Conversely, nothing above the greedy bound is reachable. -/
theorem reach_le (nums : List Nat) (M : Nat)
    (hsat : ∀ u, u < nums.length → u ≤ M → u + nums.getD u 0 ≤ M) :
    ∀ v, JReach nums v → v ≤ M := by
  intro v hv
  induction hv with
  | zero => omega
  | @step u v hu huv hle ih =>
      by_cases hun : u < nums.length
      · have := hsat u hun ih
        omega
      · have h0 : nums.getD u 0 = 0 := getD_out nums u (by omega)
        omega

theorem getD_head_zero (P : List Nat) (h : P.head? = some 0) : P.getD 0 0 = 0 := by
  cases P with
  | nil => simp at h
  | cons a t => simp at h; simp [h]

theorem getD_getLast (P : List Nat) (u : Nat) (h : P.getLast? = some u) :
    P.getD (P.length - 1) 0 = u := by
  rw [List.getLast?_eq_getElem?] at h
  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, h]

theorem ne_nil_of_head (P : List Nat) (u : Nat) (h : P.head? = some u) : P ≠ [] := by
  cases P with
  | nil => simp at h
  | cons a t => simp

theorem getD_append_left (P : List Nat) (v : Nat) (i : Nat) (hi : i < P.length) :
    (P ++ [v]).getD i 0 = P.getD i 0 := by
  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_append_left hi]

theorem getD_append_right (P : List Nat) (v : Nat) :
    (P ++ [v]).getD P.length 0 = v := by
  simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_refl P.length)]

/-- Every reachable index is the endpoint of a valid path. -/
theorem reach_to_path (nums : List Nat) (v : Nat) (hv : JReach nums v) :
    ∃ P : List Nat, P ≠ [] ∧ P.head? = some 0 ∧ P.getLast? = some v ∧
      (∀ i, i < P.length → P.getD i 0 ≤ v) ∧ jumpChain nums P := by
  induction hv with
  | zero =>
      refine ⟨[0], by simp, by simp, by simp, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro i hi
        simp at hi
        subst hi
        simp
      · intro i hi
        simp at hi
  | @step u v hu huv hle ih =>
      obtain ⟨P, hne, hhead, hlast, hbnd, hchain⟩ := ih
      have hlen : 0 < P.length := List.length_pos_of_ne_nil hne
      have hlastD : P.getD (P.length - 1) 0 = u := getD_getLast P u hlast
      refine ⟨P ++ [v], by simp, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [List.head?_append, hhead]
        rfl
      · simp
      · intro i hi
        simp only [List.length_append, List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hi
        rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i P.length with h1 | h1
        · rw [getD_append_left P v i h1]
          exact le_trans (hbnd i h1) (by omega)
        · have : i = P.length := by omega
          subst this
          rw [getD_append_right]
      · intro i hi
        simp only [List.length_append, List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at hi
        rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i (P.length - 1) with h1 | h1
        · have h2 : i < P.length := by omega
          have h3 : i + 1 < P.length := by omega
          rw [getD_append_left P v i h2, getD_append_left P v (i + 1) h3]
          exact hchain i h1
        · have h2 : i = P.length - 1 := by omega
          subst h2
          have h3 : P.length - 1 < P.length := by omega
          have h4 : P.length - 1 + 1 = P.length := by omega
          rw [getD_append_left P v _ h3, h4, getD_append_right, hlastD]
          exact ⟨huv, hle⟩

/-- Every valid path witnesses reachability of the last index. -/
theorem path_to_reach (nums : List Nat) (P : List Nat) (h : is_valid_jump_path P nums) :
    JReach nums (nums.length - 1) := by
  obtain ⟨hlen, hhead, hlast, hbnd, hchain⟩ := h
  have key : ∀ i, i < P.length → JReach nums (P.getD i 0) := by
    intro i
    induction i with
    | zero =>
        intro _
        rw [getD_head_zero P hhead]
        exact JReach.zero
    | succ n ih =>
        intro hn
        have hn' : n < P.length := by omega
        have hc := hchain n (by omega)
        simp only at hc
        exact JReach.step (ih hn') hc.1 hc.2
  have hk := key (P.length - 1) (by omega)
  rwa [getD_getLast P _ hlast] at hk

-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem can_jump_postcond_satisfied (nums : List Nat) (h_precond : can_jump_precond nums) :
    can_jump_postcond nums (can_jump nums h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  obtain ⟨hpos, -, -⟩ := h_precond
  simp only [can_jump_postcond, can_jump]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hM : nums.length - 1 ≤ jumpGo nums 0 0 := by
      simpa using h
    have hbase : ∀ k, k ≤ 0 → JReach nums k := by
      intro k hk
      have : k = 0 := by omega
      subst this
      exact JReach.zero
    have hr : JReach nums (nums.length - 1) :=
      jumpGo_reach nums 0 0 hbase _ hM
    obtain ⟨P, hne, hhead, hlast, hbnd, hchain⟩ := reach_to_path nums _ hr
    refine ⟨P, List.length_pos_of_ne_nil hne, hhead, hlast, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro i hi
      have := hbnd i hi
      omega
    · intro i hi
      simp only
      exact hchain i hi
  · rintro ⟨P, hP⟩
    have hr : JReach nums (nums.length - 1) := path_to_reach nums P hP
    have hsat : ∀ u, u < nums.length → u ≤ jumpGo nums 0 0 →
        u + nums.getD u 0 ≤ jumpGo nums 0 0 := by
      apply jumpGo_sat nums 0 0
      intro u hu
      omega
    have := reach_le nums (jumpGo nums 0 0) hsat _ hr
    simpa using this
  -- !benchmark @end proof

**LEAN VERIFIED.** Now the semantic audit.

**Algorithm (`can_jump`, code marker)** — `Nat.ble (nums.length - 1) (jumpGo nums 0 0)`. `jumpGo` is the standard O(n) greedy max-reach scan: walk `i` upward while `i` is still in range and within the current reach `r`, updating `r := max r (i + nums[i])`; stop early when `i > r` (unreachable gap) or the array ends. No brute force, no sorting, no `Nat.find`/`Classical.choose`, no `decide` on the target property (`Nat.ble` is a plain arithmetic comparison on the greedy bound).

**Helpers are genuine, not placeholders:**
- `JReach` is a real inductive reachability relation mirroring the spec's jump rule `u < v ≤ u + nums[u]`.
- `jumpChain` restates the spec's step condition verbatim.
- Both directions are proved: `jumpGo_reach` (everything ≤ the greedy bound is truly reachable, built constructively via `JReach.step`) and `jumpGo_sat` + `reach_le` (nothing above the bound is reachable). Neither is vacuous.
- `reach_to_path` *constructs* an explicit witness path (`P ++ [v]`), and `path_to_reach` extracts reachability from an arbitrary given path by induction on prefixes — so the iff is honest in both directions rather than assumed.

**Preconditions and edge cases:**
- `0 < nums.length` is used (and needed) to turn the path bound `≤ nums.length - 1` into the spec's strict `< nums.length`. The other two preconditions (`length ≤ 10000`, entries `≤ 10000`) are not needed for correctness; the proof is valid for all sizes, which is strictly stronger, not weaker.
- `nums.length = 1`: target is index 0, `jumpGo ≥ 0`, result `true`; witness path `[0]` satisfies the spec (`getLast? = some 0`). Correct.
- Leading zero, e.g. `[0, 1]`: `jumpGo` stops with `r = 0 < 1` → `false`. Correct.
- Zeros mid-array blocking progress (`[2,0,0,1]`): loop breaks when `i > r` → `false`.
- Large entries overshooting the array (`[100]`): `jumpGo` returns 100 > n-1; `JReach nums 100` is still genuinely derivable, and the path spec only constrains indices actually on the path, so no unsoundness. `getD_out` handles out-of-range indices (`nums.getD u 0 = 0`), so no phantom jumps from beyond the array.
- Values are `Nat`, so "all-negative input" cannot arise here; the corresponding degenerate case is all-zeros, covered above (`false` unless `n = 1`).

**Constraints respected:** only the four marker sections were edited, all markers preserved; no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `constant`, `partial`, `unsafe`, `extern`, or `implemented_by`. `Original.lean`, `TASK.md`, `check.sh`, `Merged.lean` untouched.

Remaining output is warnings only (three unused-variable notes, one redundant simp argument) — no errors. The check was re-run after the final edit and prints `LEAN VERIFIED`.

analysis:
The student implements the Jump Game using a standard greedy scan:

- `jumpGo nums i r` tracks the current index `i` and the furthest reachable index `r`.
- While `i` is within the array and reachable (`i ≤ r`), it updates the bound to `max r (i + nums[i])` and advances to `i + 1`.
- `can_jump` returns whether the last index is at most the final reachable bound.

This is an appropriate implementation of the required Jump Game algorithm, rather than an unrelated algorithm or a call to a pre-existing solver.

The supporting development proves both directions of the required result:
- Every index up to the greedy bound is reachable, allowing a valid path to be constructed when the algorithm returns true.
- Every valid path’s endpoint is bounded by the greedy result, so existence of a path implies that the algorithm returns true.

The answer contains substantive executable code and proofs. It does not use `sorry`, `admit`, axioms, empty bodies, or an existing verified Jump Game implementation. Mathlib is used only for ordinary definitions, lemmas, tactics, and arithmetic automation, not to bypass implementation of the algorithm.
